title: Factual Position Regarding Media Report on Disposal of Cases by CIC
subtitle: CIC Disposes of 768 Cases in August up to 12 August, Against Three Reported in Media Report
body_text:
The Central Information Commission (CIC) has taken note of a media report concerning the disposal of Second Appeals and Complaints during August 2026 and considers it necessary to place the factual position before the public.
The Commission clarifies that the figures relating to disposal of cases during August 2026, as reflected in the said news report, do not represent the actual disposal of cases by the Commission up to 12 August 2026. As against the figure of three appeals reported as having been disposed of during August, the Commission has in fact disposed of 768 cases up to 12 August 2026 in the current month . The decisions in the disposed cases are also being simultaneously dispatched by post to the concerned parties.
The Second Appeals and Complaints Portal of the Commission has been undergoing upgradation since 2 August 2026 . Consequently, the data relating to cases admitted and disposed of, which is automatically updated on the Commission’s website from the said portal, has remained updated only up to 1 August 2026 . A notice regarding the portal upgradation had already been displayed on the Commission’s website and the Second Appeals and Complaints Portal on 24 July 2026 .
It is important to clarify that the non-updation of the portal data has not affected the functioning of the Commission or the conduct of hearings . Hearings before the Commission have continued as usual during the period of portal upgradation.
The Commission therefore wishes to emphasise that the figures presently visible on its website during the portal-upgradation period should not be construed as reflecting the actual disposal of cases during August 2026 .
The upgradation of the Second Appeals and Complaints Portal is being undertaken with the objective of improving the experience of RTI applicants and other stakeholders using the Commission’s online services . The upgraded portal is intended to provide a more efficient and user-friendly digital interface for accessing and managing information relating to Second Appeals and Complaints.
The upgradation will also facilitate more efficient updating and availability of case-related information on the Commission’s website and portal, thereby making it easier for stakeholders to access current information regarding their cases.
The upgraded Second Appeals and Complaints Portal is expected to be live and operational from 17 August 2026 , following which the relevant case data is expected to be updated on the Commission’s website and portal.
The Commission remains committed to transparency and to providing accurate and verifiable information regarding its functioning. It will continue to make relevant case-disposal data available to stakeholders through its website and portal once the upgradation process is completed.
*****
NKR/AV

ministry.name: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions

enrichment.summary: The Central Information Commission (CIC) has clarified that a media report claiming only three appeals were disposed of in August 2026 was inaccurate; the Commission actually disposed of 768 cases up to 12 August 2026. The discrepancy arose because the Second Appeals and Complaints Portal, whose data auto-updates the CIC website, has been undergoing upgradation since 2 August 2026, leaving displayed figures frozen at 1 August 2026 levels. The CIC clarified that hearings and functioning continued normally during this period, and the upgraded portal is expected to go live from 17 August 2026.
enrichment.context: The Central Information Commission is the apex appellate body under the Right to Information (RTI) Act, 2005, responsible for adjudicating second appeals and complaints when public authorities deny information or fail to respond adequately. Since the CIC's website and portal serve as a key public transparency mechanism for tracking case disposal rates, discrepancies in reported statistics can affect public perception of the Commission's efficiency, especially amid recurring criticism about pendency and delays in the RTI appellate mechanism across India. This episode also highlights how technical/administrative upgrades to e-governance portals used by quasi-judicial bodies can inadvertently create public misinformation if not clearly communicated in advance, underscoring the importance of proactive official communication when digital systems are being upgraded. Vacancies and pendency in CIC and State Information Commissions have historically been raised in Parliament and by transparency advocacy groups (e.g., RTI activists, Satark Nagrik Sangathan reports) as an issue undermining the RTI regime, making the functioning and case-disposal rate of CIC a recurring subject of public and media scrutiny.

prelims_questions.question: The Central Information Commission (CIC), mentioned in the context of adjudicating second appeals, functions under which of the following Acts?
prelims_questions.explanation: The CIC is a statutory body constituted under the Right to Information Act, 2005, to hear second appeals and complaints regarding denial of information by public authorities.

prelims_questions.question: With reference to the Central Information Commission (CIC), consider the following statements: 1. It hears second appeals against decisions of the First Appellate Authority under the RTI Act. 2. Its orders are subject to appeal before the High Court under the RTI Act itself. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
prelims_questions.explanation: The CIC hears second appeals under Section 19 of the RTI Act. The RTI Act does not provide for a statutory appeal against CIC orders to the High Court, though writ jurisdiction under Article 226 can still be invoked; hence statement 2 is not correct as an RTI Act provision.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the role of the Central Information Commission in strengthening transparency and accountability in governance. What challenges affect its functioning, and how can these be addressed?
Examine how digital transformation of quasi-judicial and regulatory bodies' portals can impact public trust and transparency, citing recent examples from Indian institutions.
